newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mixed, thin exports cited.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mixed, thin exports cited.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures settled lower Friday in response to light weekly export sales, but a late short-covering rally trimmed the day's losses, CBOT traders said.
Smith Barney bought an estimated 500,000 bushels of March soybeans near the close, which triggered a short-covering rally by local traders, pit sources said.

Before the late advance, weak export sales data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture and ideas that Thursday's gains were overdone weighed heavily on soybean prices for most of the session, traders said.
"The market was overdone from yesterday (Thursday) and I knew we would have trouble holding the $7.00 (per bushel) level," one floor trader said.
USDA weekly net export sales of 293,100 tonnes were much lower than trade expectations for 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes and considered bearish for futures, floor sources said.
CBOT soybeans ended down three to up two cents per bushel with January down three cents at $6.96-1/4 and March steady at $6.98-3/4.
January came under pressure from a sharp increase in the number of deliveries, sources noted. Deliveries climbed to 1.035 million bushels, versus 615,000 on Thursday, according to CBOT data.

Some traders said that the 1996 final crop production forecast from the advisory firm Sparks Cos, pressured the market. Sparks reportedly raised its forecast for U.S. production to 2.403 billion bushels from a previous forecast of 2.367 billion bushels. Sparks officials declined to comment on the estimate.
E.D. and F. Man bought 1.2 million bushels January, and Cargill bought 500,000 March and 500,000 July.
Smith Barney bought 5.5 million bushels on the day, trade sources said.
Soybean volume was estimated at 53,000 contracts, above the 52,864 contracts traded on Thursday, according to CBOT data.
